obligation: Acquirer notice: Live Venues merchant accounts
citation: Merchant agreement (fictional term); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req. 12.10 (N71-R04)
trigger: Suspected or confirmed compromise of card data on Live Venues channels, including a common point of purchase notice
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspicion (merchant agreement term)
notify: Live Venues acquirer merchant risk contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law

obligation: Acquirer notice: Hotels and Restaurants merchant accounts
citation: Merchant agreement (fictional term); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req. 12.10 (N72-R01)
trigger: Package checkouts on the hotels tenant affected
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspicion (merchant agreement term)
notify: Hotels acquirer merchant risk contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law
notifying_entity: Hotels and Restaurants (Group PCI program director)

obligation: Acquirer notice: streaming merchant account
citation: Merchant agreement (fictional term); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req. 12.10 (N71-R04)
trigger: Streaming purchases through the affected checkout
deadline: Within 24 hours of suspicion (merchant agreement term)
notify: Streaming acquirer merchant risk contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law
notifying_entity: Ticketing and Streaming (Group PCI program director)

obligation: Visa: report the compromise event
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0 (effective 2026-06-25), Section A.1 - card brand rule applied through acquirers, not law
trigger: Evidence sufficient to raise a reasonable suspicion of, or to confirm, unauthorized access to Visa account data
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of that discovery
notify: Visa Global Risk Investigations, through each acquirer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - each merchant role and the service provider; Live Venues is a Level 1 merchant
notifying_entity: Each merchant role and the Ticketing and Streaming division as service provider

obligation: Visa: initial investigation and incident report
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.2
trigger: After notifying Visa
deadline: Within 3 calendar days of notifying Visa
notify: Visa and the acquirers
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Visa: at-risk account numbers
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.4
trigger: Discovery of compromised account data, a Visa request, or a determined window of exposure
deadline: Within 3 calendar days; provided through the acquirers or processors
notify: Visa (through the acquirers)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - payment orchestration can extract the cards used in the window
notifying_entity: Director of Payments Engineering for each merchant role

obligation: Visa: PCI forensic investigation (if required)
citation: Visa What To Do If Compromised v10.0, Section A.5
trigger: Visa requires a PCI Forensic Investigator (Level 1 and 2 merchants and service providers are more likely to be required, A.5.2)
deadline: Retain a PFI within 5 business days; initial forensic report within 5 business days of signing; final report within 10 business days of completing the investigation. The PFI must not have served the group in the past 3 years
notify: Visa and the acquirers (the PFI reports directly to Visa)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - expected for this incident
notifying_entity: Group General Counsel with the Group PCI program director
clock_starts: Visa notice that a PFI is required

obligation: Other card brands' compromise procedures
citation: Mastercard, American Express, and Discover rules - applied through the acquirers, not law
trigger: Suspected compromise of those brands' card data
deadline: Per acquirer and brand instructions (not verified here)
notify: Acquirers; card brands through the acquirers
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - follow acquirer instructions; these rules were not verified

obligation: Client notice under the client agreement
citation: 2024 client agreement (fictional terms); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req. 12.10.1 and 12.9 (N71-R04)
trigger: Security incident affecting a client's patron or card data on the TVOP
deadline: Within 24 hours for the 186 clients with that term; 72 hours under the standard agreement
notify: Each affected client's designated security contact (41 clients in this scenario)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the division is the clients' service provider

obligation: Intercompany notice to Live Venues and Hotels and Restaurants
citation: Intercompany service terms (fictional); PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req. 12.9
trigger: The TVOP incident affects the group merchants' patrons
deadline: Same day as discovery (intercompany term); on the incident bridge
notify: Live Venues and Hotels and Restaurants security and compliance leads
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Support for clients' own investigations
citation: PCI DSS v4.0.1 Req. 12.9.2 and 12.10 (N71-R04); client agreement
trigger: Client or its acquirer asks for evidence or the window of exposure
deadline: As each client's acquirer requires; respond within 2 business days (client agreement, fictional)
notify: Affected clients
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to covered entities (worked example)
trigger: The division, as third-party agent, determines a breach of a system it maintains for a client or a group merchant
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred
notify: Each affected client and group merchant (the covered entities)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the contract terms above are shorter and are used

obligation: Clients' own notices to their patrons
citation: Each state where affected individuals reside (Florida worked example 501.171(3)-(5))
trigger: Each client is the covered entity for its patrons
deadline: Per each state's law, from the client's own determination
notify: Clients' patrons and regulators
applies_at_this_tier: Clients' duty; the division supplies data and template language

obligation: State data breach notification (group merchants and streaming)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48) (N72-R04)
trigger: Breach of personal information of state residents (definitions vary)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where required; consumer reporting agencies above state counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected patrons, guests, and subscribers reside
notifying_entity: Live Venues, Hotels and Restaurants, and streaming each as the covered entity for its own customers

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of personal information of Florida residents: name with card number and security code (501.171(1)(g)1.a.(III)); email with password (1.b)
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe one occurred; 15 more days only for this individual notice if good cause is given to the Department in writing within the 30 days
notify: Each affected Florida resident, by mail or email
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 104,000 Florida residents (illustrative)

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day extension does not apply to this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Florida law enforcement delay (worked example)
trigger: A law enforcement agency determines that notice would interfere with a criminal investigation
deadline: Delay for the period the agency specifies in a written request
notify: Hold individual notices; keep the written request
applies_at_this_tier: Only if requested

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incident)
trigger: The disclosure committee determines the incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination (delay only on a U.S. Attorney General determination)
notify: SEC (public filing)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: SEC Reg S-K Item 106 annual disclosure
trigger: Annual report
deadline: With the annual report
notify: Investors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - update the description after the incident

obligation: SOC 2 report users and service auditor
trigger: Incident affecting the service organization during or after a report period
deadline: Inform the service auditor promptly; describe in the next report as the auditor requires
notify: Service auditor; user entities through the report
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the TVOP issues a SOC 2 Type 2 report

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (use the carrier breach hotline before hiring vendors)
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not law

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
trigger: Suspected criminal compromise of card data
deadline: As soon as practical (target day 0 to 1)
notify: FBI (IC3) or U.S. Secret Service field office; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering any payment to an attacker
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if an extortion demand is made. All U.S. persons. Strict liability

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). Proposed scope includes entities above the SBA size standard, which the group exceeds

notify: FinCEN
applies_at_this_tier: No - no division is a casino or card club

obligation: FCC CPNI breach notification
trigger: Breach of customer proprietary network information
deadline: As soon as practicable, no later than 7 business days after reasonable determination
notify: USSS and FBI through the FCC reporting facility

obligation: Bank service provider notification
trigger: Incident materially disrupting services to a banking organization customer for 4 or more hours
deadline: As soon as possible
notify: Each affected bank customer
applies_at_this_tier: No - the TVOP has no banking organization customers
